json.understood: You want a dated launch plan for the Fernway habit tracker, with tasks, owners and dates, built from the launch brief.
json.title: Fernway launch plan
json.objectWhy: This is a launch schedule with dates, owners and a budget, so it is a chart.

steps.title: Find facts
steps.does: Read launch-brief and pull out the launch date, the work window, the team and what each person owns, the four budget lines, and the list of things that must happen. Every point gets a word-for-word quote and its page.
steps.focus: launch date 9 February 2027; work window 4 January to 19 February 2027; four owners; $3,000 total budget in four named lines; the six must-happen items

steps.title: Write plan
steps.does: Turn the checked facts into 16 launch items. Each item has a task, an owner from the team, a start and end date inside 4 January to 19 February 2027, and the items it depends on. The four budget lines become the money column.
done: every owner is one of the four named people
every date is inside 4 January to 19 February 2027

steps.title: Second read
steps.does: Read the plan as a critical colleague: look for missing must-happen items, dates that clash with the 9 February launch, owners with too much on one day, and anything in the brief that no item covers.

steps.title: Check plan
steps.does: Code-check the plan: all 16 items have task, owner, start, end and dependencies; owners are in the team; dates sit inside the window; dependencies point at earlier items; the budget column sums to $3,000; the six must-happen points from the brief are each covered by at least one item.

plantedNotes: "Landing page design and copy" was made to end before it starts (date-order)
"Beta tester recruitment and onboarding" was given an owner who isn't on the team (owner-unknown)
"Beta feedback triage" was moved to end three weeks after the plan's window (date-out-of-range)
The budget total was raised by 150 (sum-mismatch)

unit.task: Fix bugs from beta before release

issues.text: There is no item for getting the app through app store review or any store submission step. If the habit tracker ships through an app store, review can take days and can be rejected, and nothing in the plan leaves room for that between the 7 February bug fixes and the 9 February release. This is the single most likely reason launch day slips.

The beta and the fix window contradict each other. The beta runs to 8 February (s3.5), but feedback triage stops on 6 February (s3.6) and bug fixing is a single day, 7 February (s3.7). Bugs and feedback arriving on the last two days of the beta have no route to a fix, and go/no-go on 8 February (s3.8) happens the same day the beta ends, before anyone can look at the final day's feedback. One day of fixing for a two-week beta with 30 testers is not a credible fix window.

9 February is overloaded and Leo Martins owns four of the five items that day: the online launch event, the newsletter to the waiting list, the launch post and the beta thank-you gifts (plus Sam Okoro's release). Running a live event while also sending a newsletter and a post, and getting thank-you gifts out, is more than one person can do well on launch day. Nothing says who covers Leo if part of it goes wrong.

Two dependencies point at the wrong thing. The review of the numbers (s3.16) is set to follow the short launch post (s3.12) instead of the release itself (s3.9) — the numbers that matter come from the app going live, not from a social post. The launch post (s3.12) also follows the go/no-go call (s3.8) rather than the release (s3.9), so the plan as written would let the post go out before the app is actually live.

issues.about: Nothing in the plan; brief coverage
issues.text: Several things a launch of this kind normally must cover have no item at all: analytics or instrumentation to measure sign-ups and retention (yet s3.16 reviews numbers), support and help/FAQ for new users, legal basics (privacy policy and terms, and data protection, which matters for an app holding personal habit data), payment or pricing setup if the app is paid, a plan for what to do if launch day goes wrong, and any press or media outreach. Either add items or state explicitly that these are out of scope.

The audience-building is too late to be useful. The landing page and sign-up form only go live on 2 February (s3.3), a week before launch, so the waiting list the 9 February newsletter (s3.11) depends on has almost no time to grow. There is also no item for promoting or taking registrations for the launch day event (s3.10), so the event has no way to get an audience.

Recruiting about 30 beta testers (s3.4) is a hard dependency for the beta starting 26 January (s3.5), with no buffer, no minimum number, and no fallback if recruitment falls short. Whoever owns this has no room to recover.

Two things need confirming against the brief. First, every date is in 2027 — check the brief actually says 2027, because if not, the entire plan is one year out. Second, the total of 3,000 has no stated link to the brief's budget, and the landing page build (s3.3) carries a budget of 0 with no note on why. There is also no contingency line anywhere in the budget for a launch that has zero slack in the schedule.

json.verdict: Not ready to take to the person as-is. The launch day itself and the go/no-go are scheduled, but the plan has no slack, no app store step, no way to fix bugs found late in the beta, and no items for analytics, support or legal. Fix the seven major points before presenting.

Fix bugs the beta found before release
Release the app on launch day

Paid posts in the first two weeks
Review of the numbers one week after launch
